OVERVIEW

This document describes the rate limiting behavior applied to all external API
endpoints exposed by the Acme Logistics Platform. It is intended for internal
engineering reference and for inclusion in customer-facing API documentation
where noted.

STANDARD RATE LIMITS

Free-tier API keys are limited to 60 requests per minute and 10,000 requests per
day, calculated on a rolling window basis rather than a fixed calendar window.
Professional-tier API keys are limited to 600 requests per minute and 200,000
requests per day. Enterprise-tier customers negotiate custom limits directly
with their account manager, recorded in the account configuration table rather
than enforced through the standard tier system.

RATE LIMIT HEADERS

Every API response includes three headers describing the caller's current rate
limit status: X-RateLimit-Limit (the maximum allowed requests in the current
window), X-RateLimit-Remaining (requests remaining in the current window), and
X-RateLimit-Reset (a Unix timestamp indicating when the current window resets).
Clients should treat these headers as authoritative and adjust request pacing
accordingly rather than relying on client-side request counting.

EXCEEDING RATE LIMITS

Requests exceeding the caller's rate limit receive an HTTP 429 status code with
a Retry-After header indicating the minimum number of seconds to wait before
retrying. Repeated violations (more than 10 rate-limit rejections within a
5-minute window) trigger a temporary 15-minute full suspension of the API key,
independent of the normal per-minute and per-day limits.

BURST ALLOWANCE

Professional and Enterprise tier keys receive a burst allowance equal to 20% of
their per-minute limit, permitting short traffic spikes without triggering a
429 response, provided the caller's rolling-window average remains within the
standard limit over any 60-second period.

ENDPOINT-SPECIFIC OVERRIDES

Some endpoints carry stricter limits than the account-level default due to
higher backend processing cost. The bulk shipment creation endpoint
(/v2/shipments/bulk) is limited to 10 requests per minute regardless of account
tier, since each request may create up to 500 individual shipment records. The
route optimization endpoint (/v2/routes/optimize) is limited to 30 requests per
minute per account, since each request triggers a computationally expensive
optimization run.

WEBHOOK DELIVERY RATE LIMITS

Outbound webhook deliveries from Acme's platform to a customer's registered
endpoint are not subject to the same rate limits as inbound API calls. However,
if a customer's webhook endpoint returns 5 consecutive failures (non-2xx
responses or timeouts exceeding 10 seconds), webhook delivery to that endpoint
is automatically paused for 30 minutes before automatic retry resumes.

REQUESTING A LIMIT INCREASE

Customers on the Professional tier may request a temporary or permanent rate
limit increase by submitting a request through the developer portal, which is
reviewed by the platform engineering team within 2 business days. Temporary
increases (for planned traffic events such as a product launch) are typically
approved within 24 hours given at least 5 business days' advance notice.

CHANGE HISTORY

Version 1.4 (January 2026): Added endpoint-specific override section for bulk
shipment creation and route optimization endpoints, following repeated support
tickets about unexpected 429 responses on those two endpoints specifically.

Version 1.3 (September 2025): Introduced the burst allowance for Professional
and Enterprise tiers, replacing the previous strict per-minute cap with no
burst tolerance.

Version 1.2 (April 2025): Changed rate limit windows from fixed calendar
windows to rolling windows, following customer feedback that fixed windows
created unpredictable "reset spikes" at the top of each minute.

Acme Logistics Platform — Product Specification
Document Version: 2.3 | Last Updated: January 2026
1. Overview

The Acme Logistics Platform is a cloud-based system for route optimization, shipment tracking, and warehouse inventory management. This document specifies the core functional requirements for the platform's v2.3 release, targeted at mid-market logistics companies operating 5-50 vehicle fleets.
2. Route Optimization Module
2.1 Optimization Algorithm

The route optimization engine uses a constrained vehicle routing algorithm that accounts for delivery time windows, vehicle capacity, and driver working-hour limits. Routes are recalculated automatically whenever a new order is added within 30 minutes of the current dispatch window, and manually on-demand at any other time.
2.2 Real-Time Traffic Integration

Route calculations incorporate real-time traffic data refreshed every 5 minutes during active delivery windows. If traffic data becomes unavailable, the system falls back to historical average travel times for the given route segment and time of day, and flags affected routes as 'estimated' in the dispatcher UI.
3. Shipment Tracking Module
3.1 Status Update Frequency

Shipment status updates are pushed to the customer-facing tracking portal within 60 seconds of a driver marking a delivery event (picked up, in transit, delivered, or exception) in the driver mobile app. Customers receive an SMS notification for delivery and exception events only, not for routine in-transit updates.
3.2 Exception Handling

Delivery exceptions (failed delivery, damaged package, customer unavailable) require the driver to select a reason code and optionally attach a photo before the exception can be submitted. Exceptions automatically create a follow-up task assigned to the dispatcher on duty, due within 4 business hours.
4. Warehouse Inventory Module
4.1 Stock Level Thresholds

Each SKU has a configurable low-stock threshold. When on-hand quantity falls below this threshold, the system generates a replenishment alert visible on the warehouse manager's dashboard and, if enabled, sends an automated email to the designated procurement contact for that SKU.
4.2 Cycle Counting

The platform supports scheduled cycle counts at the SKU or bin-location level. Discrepancies between system-recorded and physically counted quantities exceeding a 2% variance threshold automatically flag the SKU for a full recount before the adjusted quantity is accepted into the system of record.
5. Non-Functional Requirements
6. Out of Scope for v2.3

The following capabilities are explicitly out of scope for this release and are tracked separately on the v3.0 roadmap: multi-warehouse transfer optimization, predictive maintenance alerts for fleet vehicles, and customer-facing route ETA sharing via public API. Any customer requests for these capabilities should be logged in the product feedback tracker rather than treated as a defect.

Preface
These are the class notes I took for ESA Mograne : Introduction to Machine Learning and
Deep Learning. These notes are part of a course designed for students in agronomy (rural
economics and vegetable production). The course, focused on deep learning, assumes that
students have little to no background in machine learning or advanced theoretical ma-
thematics. To make these concepts more accessible, I decided to introduce foundational
machine learning concepts and then delve into deep learning, describing some algorithms
without getting into detailed mathematical demonstrations. Additionally, I have provided
a GitHub repository1 containing code, notebooks, and examples relevant to agronomy,
which will help students better understand and apply these concepts.

Machine learning (ML) involves programming computers to enhance their performance
using example data or past experiences. This process entails defining a model with spe-
cific parameters and employing a computer program to optimize these parameters with
training data or prior experiences. The resulting model can be used for making future
predictions (predictive) or extracting insights from data (descriptive), or both. The term
’Machine Learning’ was introduced by Arthur Samuel, a pioneer in computer gaming and
